## Findings

**1. HIGH — `apps/web/app/layout.tsx` (+ `apps/web/tailwind.config.ts`, `apps/web/app/globals.css`) — Inter/JetBrains Mono are declared but never actually loaded, breaking the locked design-system typography rule**

Evidence:
- This diff removes the only font source in the app: `git diff -- apps/web/app/layout.tsx` shows the `<head>` block with the Google Fonts `<link>` (Inter + JetBrains Mono) deleted, with nothing added in its place.
- `apps/web/tailwind.config.ts:23-24` still declares `sans: ['Inter', 'system-ui', 'sans-serif']` and `mono: ['"JetBrains Mono"', 'ui-monospace', 'monospace']`.
- No replacement font source exists anywhere: no `next/font` import in `layout.tsx`, no `@font-face` in `apps/web/app/globals.css`, no local font files (`find apps/web -iname "*.woff*" -o -iname "*.ttf"` → empty), no font package in `apps/web/package.json` or `node_modules`.
- Result: since `'Inter'` and `'"JetBrains Mono"'` are not installed as system fonts on any typical machine, every browser silently falls through to `system-ui`/`ui-monospace` — the app never renders the mandated typefaces.
- This directly violates AGENTS.md's "Locked. Do not improvise" design system section ("Inter 400/500 for UI text. JetBrains Mono for filenames and paths") and SPEC.md acceptance criterion #3 ("camera-ready and complies with every locked design-system rule"), while the CDN-removal itself was correct per scope-in item #2 ("no external CDN/design dependency"). The correct fix was self-hosting (e.g. `next/font/google`, which bundles at build time with no runtime network call), not deleting the only font source.

Required fix: self-host Inter and JetBrains Mono (e.g. via `next/font/google` or bundled static font files under `apps/web/public`) so the charte typefaces actually render, while keeping zero external CDN calls at runtime.

**2. MEDIUM — `apps/web/app/demo/demo-workspace.tsx:209`, `apps/web/components/proposal-card.tsx:139,80,115`, `apps/web/app/dashboard/layout.tsx:65` — text-contrast utilities fail WCAG AA 4.5:1 on white/paper backgrounds**

Evidence (WCAG relative-luminance contrast math against `ink #0A0A0A` alpha-blended over `#FFFFFF`):
- `text-ink/45` (demo-workspace.tsx:209, timestamp) → blended ≈ rgb(145,145,145) → contrast ≈ **3.15:1**
- `text-ink/50` (proposal-card.tsx:139, dialog close button) → blended ≈ rgb(133,133,133) → contrast ≈ **3.69:1**
- `text-ink/55` (proposal-card.tsx:80,115, source label / error subtext) → contrast ≈ **4.43:1**, just under threshold
- `text-ink/40` (dashboard/layout.tsx:65, chevron icon area) → contrast ≈ **2.9:1**
- All are normal-weight text at 12–14px (`text-xs`/`text-sm`), which requires 4.5:1 under WCAG AA; none of these meet it (minimum opacity needed is ≈56%, i.e. `text-ink/60` or higher).
- Directly violates AGENTS.md: "Text contrast must be verified, not assumed."

Required fix: raise these instances to `text-ink/60` or darker (or otherwise verify against the actual computed background, since `bg-paper` is even lighter than white and would fail worse) and re-verify with a contrast checker before claiming compliance.
